title: Indra walks back: the dreamer isn't the self
hook: twice Indra finds the flaw in his teacher's answer, and twice he walks back, firewood in hand
carry: the self is not the dreamer
tomorrow: deep sleep, and the one who sees

segments.voice: Yesterday: Prajapati, and two students who took a reflection in a pan of water for the self. Your line was the reflection isn't you. Week five of year two begins.

Picture the king of the gods on a road, halfway home, standing still. Indra has just spent thirty-two years with his teacher, Prajapati, and he left happy: the self, he was told, is the one you see in a pan of water. Then, a few steps from home, the answer cracks. He has the choice every student since has had: pretend it made sense, or walk back and say, I don't understand yet.
screen: `HALFWAY HOME, THE ANSWER CRACKS.` → `PRETEND IT MADE SENSE?` → `OR WALK BACK?`

segments.voice: On the road, Indra thinks it through. If the self is that reflection, then when the body is well dressed, it's well dressed. When the body is blind, it's blind. When the body dies, it dies. I see nothing good in this. So he turns around and walks back to Prajapati with firewood in his hands, samit-pani, the sign of a student asking to be taught. You left content, Prajapati says. Why are you back? Indra tells him. It is so, Prajapati answers. Live here another thirty-two years. The king of the gods signs up for thirty-two more years because one answer didn't hold. Then the next teaching: the one who moves about happily in dreams, that is the self. Better, surely. The dreamer isn't blind when the body is blind. Indra leaves, content again. And again, on the road, the doubt comes. In dreams, it's as if someone is chasing him. It's as if he feels pain. He even weeps, as it were. I see nothing good in this either. So, once more, he turns around. Here's what Hindus take from this. The atman, the self, isn't the body, and it isn't the dreamer either. The Upanishads count three states we pass through, waking, dream and deep sleep, and they look for the self that's there through all three. And the way you find it is the old teacher and student way: you bring your doubt back, firewood in hand, as many times as it takes.
screen: `IF THE BODY IS BLIND, SO IS IT.` · `BACK, WITH FIREWOOD IN HAND.` · `THE DREAMER: SURELY THIS ONE?` · `BUT IN DREAMS, HE WEEPS.` · then, large: `THE SELF IS NOT THE DREAMER.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and notice the pictures that start on their own, a memory, a plan, a little scene, like a dream but awake. Don't follow them; notice that a picture is showing and something is aware of it, and when a scene pulls you in, step back to the one aware of the dream.
Indra returns. The king of the gods walks back to his teacher, twice, because the reflection and then the dreamer didn't hold up.
Your line: the self is not the dreamer. Tomorrow, Indra goes back a third time. See you then.

howItsDone: Students in many Hindu traditions return to their teacher with questions again and again; carrying firewood (samit-pani) is the traditional sign of approaching a teacher as a student.

chat.meaning: Prajapati first called the dreamer the self, but Indra saw that the dreamer is chased and weeps. Hindus look for the self beneath waking, dream and sleep: the one aware of them all.
